editorial:
Imagine being completely alone in a strange country where you do not speak the language and have no one to turn to. You get a real sense of this struggle through Loh Kiwan, a North Korean defector living in Belgium. He is just trying to survive and get legal papers so he can stay. While he is fighting for his life, he meets a woman who has everything on paper but feels empty and hopeless inside. The vibe is very heavy and sad, but it is also deeply human because it shows how two broken people can find a reason to keep going when they lean on each other.

What really makes this work is the acting; the lead actors make you feel every bit of their pain and longing. The pacing is slow, which might feel like a drag if you want action, but it helps you feel the loneliness of the characters. If you enjoy stories about survival and unexpected love, you should definitely give this a try.
endingExplained: In the end, Kiwan and the woman form a deep bond that gives them both a reason to survive. After a lot of suffering and legal battles, Kiwan finally finds a path toward stability. The movie wraps up by showing that while their trauma will not just go away, they no longer have to face the world alone. They choose to support each other, ending the story on a hopeful note about healing and new beginnings.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about overcoming hardship and finding love in dark places.
